# Holon SaaS Framework
**Version:** 1.0.0 **Java:** 21 (LTS) **Spring Boot:** 4.0.4 **Vaadin:** 25.1.0 (optional — only `tenant-vaadin` and `tenant-admin` modules require it)
The **Holon SaaS Framework** provides a complete multi-tenant platform for building production-ready SaaS applications with Spring Boot. It was extracted from the `holon-vaadin-flow` project as an independent, reusable library.
---
## Modules
| Module | Artifact ID | Description | |--------|-------------|-------------| | `tenant-core` | `holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-core` | Core tenant model: `TenantDetails`, `TenantContext`, `TenantPlan`, `TenantFeature`, lifecycle events | | `tenant-data` | `holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-data` | Multi-tenant datasource routing, per-tenant Flyway migrations, schema isolation | | `tenant-security` | `holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-security` | Spring Security integration: `TenantAwareUserDetails`, `TenantIsolationFilter`, AOP guards | | `tenant-onboarding` | `holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-onboarding` | Tenant provisioning pipeline with hooks and event publishing | | `tenant-audit` | `holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-audit` | `@AuditAction` AOP support, in-memory and pluggable audit storage | | `tenant-settings` | `holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-settings` | Per-tenant key/value settings with typed access | | `tenant-limits` | `holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-limits` | `@RateLimit` / `@TenantLimit` AOP enforcement | | `tenant-users` | `holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-users` | Tenant user management: invite, activate, suspend, roles | | `tenant-billing` | `holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-billing` | Subscription and invoice management | | `tenant-vaadin` | `holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-vaadin` | Vaadin 25 integration: `TenantNavigationGuard`, `TenantSession`, async task security | | `tenant-admin` | `holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-admin` | Super-admin Vaadin UI components for tenant management | | `starter-saas` | `holon-starter-vaadin-flow-saas` | Spring Boot auto-configuration starter for all modules | | `bom` | `holon-saas-bom` | Bill of Materials — import to manage all module versions |
---
## Quick Start
### BOM Import (recommended) Add the BOM to your project's `<dependencyManagement>`: ```xml <dependencyManagement> <dependencies> <dependency> <groupId>com.holon-platform.saas</groupId> <artifactId>holon-saas-bom</artifactId> <version>1.0.0</version> <type>pom</type> <scope>import</scope> </dependency> </dependencies> </dependencyManagement> ```
### All-in-one Starter ```xml <dependency> <groupId>com.holon-platform.saas</groupId> <artifactId>holon-starter-vaadin-flow-saas</artifactId> <version>1.0.0</version> </dependency> ``` Then add the Spring Boot starters your application needs (e.g., `spring-boot-starter-web`, `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa`, `spring-boot-starter-security`).
### Cherry-pick individual modules ```xml <!-- Core (always required) --> <dependency> <groupId>com.holon-platform.saas</groupId> <artifactId>holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-core</artifactId> </dependency>
<!-- Add as needed --> <dependency> <groupId>com.holon-platform.saas</groupId> <artifactId>holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-security</artifactId> </dependency> <dependency> <groupId>com.holon-platform.saas</groupId> <artifactId>holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-data</artifactId> </dependency> ```
---
## Architecture
``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Your SaaS Application │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ holon-starter-vaadin-flow-saas │ │ ┌──────────┐ ┌─────────┐ │ │ │ tenant │ │ tenant │ ← Vaadin │ │ │ -admin │ │ -vaadin │ Layer │ │ └──────────┘ └─────────┘ │ │ ┌──────────┐ ┌─────────┐ ┌─────────┐│ │ │ security │ │ audit │ │ billing ││ │ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └─────────┘│ │ ┌──────────┐ ┌─────────┐ ┌─────────┐│ │ │ users │ │settings │ │ limits ││ │ └──────────┘ └─────────┘ └─────────┘│ │ ┌──────────┐ ┌───────────────────────┐│ │ │ data │ │ onboarding ││ │ └──────────┘ └───────────────────────┘│ │ ┌──────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ tenant-core │ │ └──────────────────────────────────────┘ └─────────────────────────────────────────┘ ```
---
## Key Concepts
### Tenant Isolation Every tenant gets its own database schema (via `tenant-data`) and Spring Security context isolation (via `tenant-security`). The `TenantIsolationFilter` (order -50) blocks cross-tenant access with HTTP 403.
### Plan-Based Access Control ```java // Protect a service method @RequiresPlan(TenantPlan.PROFESSIONAL) public void exportReports() { ... }
// Protect a Vaadin view @Route("reports") @TenantPlanRequired(minimum = TenantPlan.PROFESSIONAL) public class ReportsView extends Div { ... } ```
### Feature Flags ```java @CheckTenantFeature(TenantFeature.ADVANCED_REPORTS) public Report generateAdvancedReport() { ... } ```
### Tenant Onboarding ```java @Autowired TenantOnboardingService onboarding;
onboarding.onboard(TenantOnboardingRequest.builder() .tenantId("acme") .plan(TenantPlan.PROFESSIONAL) .ownerEmail("owner@acme.com") .build()); ```
### Audit Trail ```java @AuditAction(action = "USER_LOGIN", description = "User logged in") public void login(String userId) { ... } ```
### Rate Limiting ```java @RateLimit(limit = 100, window = 60, unit = TimeUnit.SECONDS) public void apiEndpoint() { ... } ```
---
## Building
```bash # Build and install mvn clean install
# Run tests only mvn test
# Skip tests mvn install -DskipTests ```
---
## Dependency on holon-vaadin-flow
The `tenant-vaadin` and `tenant-admin` modules depend on: - `com.holon-platform.vaadin:holon-vaadin-flow:10.0.0` - `com.holon-platform.vaadin:holon-vaadin-flow-spring-boot:10.0.0`
These are resolved from your local Maven repository. Build `holon-vaadin-flow` first: ```bash cd ../holon-vaadin-flow mvn install -DskipTests ```
---
## Migration from holon-vaadin-flow
If you were previously depending on tenant modules from `holon-vaadin-flow`, update your dependency coordinates:
| Old (holon-vaadin-flow) | New (holon-saas) | |-------------------------|------------------| | `com.holon-platform.vaadin:holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-core:10.0.0` | `com.holon-platform.saas:holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-core:1.0.0` | | `com.holon-platform.vaadin:holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-security:10.0.0` | `com.holon-platform.saas:holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-security:1.0.0` | | … | … | | `com.holon-platform.vaadin:holon-vaadin-flow-bom:10.0.0` | `com.holon-platform.saas:holon-saas-bom:1.0.0` |
Artifact IDs are **unchanged** — only the `groupId` and `version` change. No Java source code changes are required.
## CRM walkthrough moved
The long CRM walkthrough has been moved to a dedicated guide:
- [`docs/multi-tenant-crm-guide.md`](docs/multi-tenant-crm-guide.md)
Keep `README.md` for the project overview, module list, quick start, and migration notes.

# Adopting the WhatsApp Integration in a New App
This document is a step-by-step guide for integrating the `holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-whatsapp` module into a **new** Spring Boot + Vaadin multi-tenant application.
---
## 1. Add the dependency
### Option A — You already use `holon-starter-vaadin-flow-saas`
The starter lists `tenant-whatsapp` as **optional**. Just declare it explicitly:
```xml <!-- pom.xml --> <dependencies>
<!-- Pulls in all other SaaS modules --> <dependency> <groupId>com.holon-platform.saas</groupId> <artifactId>holon-starter-vaadin-flow-saas</artifactId> </dependency>
<!-- ✅ Add this — WhatsApp integration --> <dependency> <groupId>com.holon-platform.saas</groupId> <artifactId>holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-whatsapp</artifactId> </dependency>
</dependencies> ```
**Version** is managed by the parent BOM (`holon-saas-root`) — no `<version>` tag needed.
---
### Option B — Standalone (no holon-starter)
```xml <dependencies>
<dependency> <groupId>com.holon-platform.saas</groupId> <artifactId>holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-whatsapp</artifactId> <version>1.0.0</version> <!-- pin version explicitly --> </dependency>
<!-- Required transitive deps if not using the starter --> <dependency> <groupId>com.holon-platform.saas</groupId> <artifactId>holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-core</artifactId> <version>1.0.0</version> </dependency> <dependency> <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId> <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId> </dependency> <dependency> <groupId>com.fasterxml.jackson.core</groupId> <artifactId>jackson-databind</artifactId> </dependency>
</dependencies> ```
---
## 2. Configure `application.properties`
### Minimal — Demo / development mode (no real WhatsApp account)
```properties # WhatsApp integration is ON by default; no credentials → DEMO mode # Messages are logged only; no real API calls are made. holon.tenant.whatsapp.default-tenant-id=my-app holon.tenant.whatsapp.webhook.verify-token=change-me ```
The app starts, the Vaadin UI at `/whatsapp` is fully functional, and all sends are logged (no Meta Cloud API calls, no charge).
---
### Production — Connected to Meta WhatsApp Cloud API
```properties # ── Meta credentials ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── holon.tenant.whatsapp.shared.access-token=EAAG... # System User token holon.tenant.whatsapp.shared.phone-number-id=12345678901 # Phone Number ID holon.tenant.whatsapp.shared.waba-id=98765432109 # WABA ID
# ── Webhook ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── # Must match "Verify Token" you enter in the Meta App Dashboard → Webhooks holon.tenant.whatsapp.webhook.verify-token=my-secret-token
# ── Mode ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── # SHARED = one WABA phone, all tenants receive/send on the same number # DEDICATED = each tenant has its own WABA (implement TenantWhatsAppCredentialsProvider) holon.tenant.whatsapp.mode=SHARED
# ── Fallback tenant (SHARED mode only) ─────────────────────────────────────── # Which tenantId to assign inbound webhook events to when not specified in the URL holon.tenant.whatsapp.default-tenant-id=my-tenant-id
# ── Plan-based marketing quotas (optional overrides) ───────────────────────── holon.tenant.whatsapp.plan-marketing-limits.FREE=50 holon.tenant.whatsapp.plan-marketing-limits.STARTER=200 holon.tenant.whatsapp.plan-marketing-limits.PROFESSIONAL=2000 holon.tenant.whatsapp.plan-marketing-limits.ENTERPRISE=-1 ```
---
## 3. What you get for free (zero additional code)
As soon as the dependency is on the classpath, Spring Boot's auto-configuration (`TenantWhatsAppAutoConfiguration`) registers the following beans automatically:
| Bean | Description | |---|---| | `ConversationWindowTracker` | In-memory tracker of 24-hour free service windows — the core cost-saving component | | `TenantWhatsAppService` (default impl) | In-memory service; sends via Meta Cloud API when credentials are set | | `WhatsAppWebhookController` | `GET /webhook/whatsapp` (Meta verification) + `POST /webhook/whatsapp` (events) |
**Vaadin UI is also registered automatically:**
| Route | Description | |---|---| | `/whatsapp` | Cost dashboard — KPI cards, free/paid ratio, quick-send | | `/whatsapp/conversations` | Active service windows + lazy message history | | `/whatsapp/templates` | All WABA templates with cost colour-coding | | `/whatsapp/settings` | Credentials status + cost guide |
All views are accessible immediately at `http://localhost:8080/whatsapp`.
---
## 4. Add WhatsApp to your Vaadin navigation menu
In your main `AppLayout`, add a `SideNavItem` pointing to the dashboard:
```java import com.holonplatform.multitenant.whatsapp.ui.views.WhatsAppDashboardView; import com.vaadin.flow.component.sidenav.SideNavItem; import com.vaadin.flow.component.icon.VaadinIcon;
// Inside your layout constructor: SideNavItem whatsappItem = new SideNavItem( "WhatsApp", WhatsAppDashboardView.class, VaadinIcon.MOBILE.create() ); nav.addItem(whatsappItem); ```
Or point to the entire WhatsApp shell layout (if you want the WhatsApp sub-navigation):
```java // Just link to the management section from a button or router link Anchor link = new Anchor("/whatsapp", "WhatsApp Management →"); ```
---
## 5. Send a WhatsApp message from your own code
Inject `TenantWhatsAppService` anywhere in your Spring beans or Vaadin views:
```java @Service public class OrderService {
private final TenantWhatsAppService whatsApp;
public OrderService(TenantWhatsAppService whatsApp) { this.whatsApp = whatsApp; }
public void notifyShipped(String tenantId, String customerPhone, String orderNumber) { // Cost-optimal path: // 1. If a free service window is open → sends as a free plain-text reply // 2. If no window → uses the 'order_shipped' UTILITY template (also free) if (whatsApp.hasOpenServiceWindow(tenantId, customerPhone)) { whatsApp.sendTextMessage(tenantId, customerPhone, "Your order " + orderNumber + " has shipped! "); } else { whatsApp.sendTemplateMessage(tenantId, customerPhone, "order_shipped", "en_US", Map.of("1", orderNumber, "2", "tomorrow")); } } } ```
---
## 6. Replace the in-memory implementation with a persistent one
The default `InMemoryTenantWhatsAppService` stores messages in `ConcurrentHashMap`. For production, implement `TenantWhatsAppService` and expose it as a `@Service` bean — `@ConditionalOnMissingBean` ensures yours replaces the default automatically:
```java @Service public class JpaTenantWhatsAppService implements TenantWhatsAppService {
private final WhatsAppMessageRepository repo; // your JPA repo private final ConversationWindowTracker windowTracker; // inject — still managed by auto-config private final TenantWhatsAppProperties properties; // inject — auto-configured
@Override public WhatsAppMessage sendTextMessage(String tenantId, String to, String text) { boolean freeWindow = windowTracker.hasOpenFreeWindow(tenantId, to); // … build message, call Meta API, persist to DB … }
@Override public List<WhatsAppMessage> listMessages(String tenantId, int offset, int limit) { return repo.findByTenantIdOrderByCreatedAtDesc(tenantId, PageRequest.of(offset / limit, limit)).getContent(); }
// … implement remaining interface methods … } ```
---
## 7. Handle per-tenant WABA credentials (DEDICATED mode)
When each tenant has their own Meta account:
```properties holon.tenant.whatsapp.mode=DEDICATED ```
Then in your `TenantWhatsAppService` implementation, use `TenantContext` to look up the tenant's credentials at send time:
```java private WhatsAppCloudApiClient clientFor(String tenantId) { // Load credentials from DB/secrets vault for this tenant TenantWabaCredentials creds = credentialsRepo.findByTenantId(tenantId) .orElseThrow(() -> new WhatsAppNotConfiguredException(tenantId)); return new WhatsAppCloudApiClient( creds.phoneNumberId(), creds.wabaId(), creds.accessToken() ); } ```
For per-tenant webhook routing, Meta calls `POST /webhook/whatsapp/{tenantId}` — the controller already handles this route variant out of the box.
---
## 8. Register the webhook in Meta Business Manager
1. Go to **Meta for Developers** → your App → **WhatsApp → Configuration** 2. Under **Webhooks**, click **Edit** 3. Set: - **Callback URL**: `https://<your-public-domain>/webhook/whatsapp` - **Verify Token**: must match `holon.tenant.whatsapp.webhook.verify-token` 4. Subscribe to **messages** field 5. Click **Verify and Save**
> **Local development**: Use [ngrok](https://ngrok.com/) or [localtunnel](https://localtunnel.me/) > to expose your local port 8080: `ngrok http 8080` > Then set the ngrok URL as the Callback URL.
---
## 9. Obtain Meta credentials (one-time setup)
| Step | Where | |---|---| | Create a Meta App | [developers.facebook.com](https://developers.facebook.com) → **My Apps → Create App** → type **Business** | | Add WhatsApp product | App Dashboard → **Add Product → WhatsApp** | | Get Phone Number ID | WhatsApp → **API Setup** → copy **Phone number ID** | | Get WABA ID | WhatsApp → **API Setup** → copy **WhatsApp Business Account ID** | | Create System User token | **Business Settings → System Users → Add → Assign to WABA (MANAGE permission) → Generate Token** |
The System User token **never expires** (set to "Standard" token type) and is the recommended approach for production. Never use a personal user access token.
---
## 10. Cost optimisation — what happens automatically
You don't need to do anything special to benefit from cost savings. The framework's `ConversationWindowTracker` runs the following logic on every send:
``` Customer sends you a WhatsApp message ↓ Webhook fires → registerInboundMessage(tenantId, phone) ↓ 24-hour free service window opens in memory ↓ Your app calls service.sendTextMessage(tenantId, phone, "Hello!") ↓ hasOpenFreeWindow() == true → plain TEXT reply → ✅ FREE ↓ (if window expired / first contact) Service picks UTILITY template (also FREE since 2024) Only MARKETING templates are charged; plan quota enforced ```
**Free categories** (no Meta charge): - `SERVICE` — reply within open 24-h customer window - `UTILITY` — order confirmations, shipping, reminders, alerts
**Charged categories**: - `MARKETING` — promotions, re-engagement (gated by plan quota) - `AUTHENTICATION` — OTP / verification codes
---
## Quick-start checklist
``` ☐ 1. Add holon-vaadin-flow-tenant-whatsapp to pom.xml ☐ 2. Set holon.tenant.whatsapp.webhook.verify-token in application.properties ☐ 3. (Optional) Set shared.access-token / phone-number-id / waba-id for live API ☐ 4. (Optional) Add WhatsApp nav item in your AppLayout ☐ 5. (Optional) Implement TenantWhatsAppService to persist messages in DB ☐ 6. Register webhook URL in Meta Business Manager ☐ 7. Start app → navigate to /whatsapp to see the dashboard ```

# Maven Wrapper script for POSIX shells # Requires: Java 17+, curl or wget
set -e
MAVEN_WRAPPER_PROPERTIES=".mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties"
if [ -f "$MAVEN_WRAPPER_PROPERTIES" ]; then DISTRIBUTION_URL=$(grep -m 1 "^distributionUrl" "$MAVEN_WRAPPER_PROPERTIES" | cut -d'=' -f2-) fi
WRAPPER_JAR=".mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.jar" MAVEN_HOME="${HOME}/.m2/wrapper/dists/$(basename "$DISTRIBUTION_URL" -bin.zip)"
if [ ! -d "$MAVEN_HOME" ]; then echo "Downloading Maven from $DISTRIBUTION_URL" mkdir -p "$MAVEN_HOME" if command -v curl > /dev/null 2>&1; then curl -fsSL -o "/tmp/maven.zip" "$DISTRIBUTION_URL" else wget -q -O "/tmp/maven.zip" "$DISTRIBUTION_URL" fi unzip -q "/tmp/maven.zip" -d "$MAVEN_HOME" rm "/tmp/maven.zip" fi
MVN_EXEC=$(find "$MAVEN_HOME" -name "mvn" -type f | head -1) exec "$MVN_EXEC" "$@"

package com.holonplatform.multitenant.whatsapp; import java.math.BigDecimal; import java.time.LocalDate; import java.time.YearMonth; import java.util.List; import java.util.Map; import java.util.Optional; /** * Primary API for multi-tenant WhatsApp Business messaging. * *

Cost-optimisation contract

* Implementations MUST implement the following strategy to minimise Meta billing: *
    *
  1. Window-first routing – before sending any message, check * {@link #hasOpenServiceWindow(String, String)}. If a free 24-hour window * is open, plain TEXT is sent (cheapest path).
    2. *
  2. Utility templates before marketing – when no window is open, prefer * {@link WhatsAppConversationType#UTILITY} templates (free) over * {@link WhatsAppConversationType#MARKETING} (charged).
    3. *
  3. Plan-based quota enforcement – marketing sends are blocked once the * tenant's monthly marketing quota (determined by {@link com.holonplatform.multitenant.TenantPlan}) * is reached. Use {@link #getUsageStats(String, YearMonth)} to monitor usage.
    4. *
  4. Rate limiting – the default implementation integrates with * {@code TenantRateLimiter} to prevent burst sends.
    5. *
*/ public interface TenantWhatsAppService { // ─── Sending ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── /** * Sends a plain-text message to a customer phone number. *

* The method automatically picks the cheapest path: * if a service window is open the message is sent as a free reply; * otherwise it queues a UTILITY template as a fallback. *

* * @param tenantId tenant identifier * @param to recipient phone in E.164 format * @param text message text (max 4 096 characters) * @return the persisted {@link WhatsAppMessage} */ WhatsAppMessage sendTextMessage(String tenantId, String to, String text); /** * Sends a pre-approved message template. * * @param tenantId tenant identifier * @param to recipient phone in E.164 format * @param templateName template name as registered in Meta Business Manager * @param language BCP-47 language code (e.g. {@code "en_US"}) * @param params ordered substitution variables ({{1}}, {{2}}, …) * @return the persisted {@link WhatsAppMessage} */ WhatsAppMessage sendTemplateMessage(String tenantId, String to, String templateName, String language, Map params); /** * Sends a media message (image, document, audio, video). * * @param tenantId tenant identifier * @param to recipient phone in E.164 format * @param mediaType must be one of IMAGE, DOCUMENT, AUDIO, VIDEO * @param mediaUrl public HTTPS URL or Meta media-id * @param caption optional caption (ignored for AUDIO) * @return the persisted {@link WhatsAppMessage} */ WhatsAppMessage sendMediaMessage(String tenantId, String to, WhatsAppMessageType mediaType, String mediaUrl, String caption); // ─── Business document sending ──────────────────────────────────────────── /** * Sends a high-level business document message (invoice, quotation, payment reminder…). * *

The implementation automatically:

*
    *
  1. Selects the appropriate UTILITY template (free) for the * {@link WhatsAppBusinessMessageType}.
    2. *
  2. If a 24-hour service window is open for the recipient, sends a plain-text * summary instead (also free and even cheaper).
    3. *
  3. If {@link WhatsAppBusinessMessage#documentUrl()} is set, sends the PDF * as a WhatsApp DOCUMENT attachment in addition to the text/template.
    4. *
* * @param tenantId tenant identifier * @param message business message descriptor built via {@link WhatsAppBusinessMessage#invoice()}, etc. * @return the persisted {@link WhatsAppMessage} for the text/template notification * (the document attachment, if sent, is returned by the list in * {@link WhatsAppBusinessSendResult#messages()}) */ WhatsAppBusinessSendResult sendBusinessMessage(String tenantId, WhatsAppBusinessMessage message); /** * Shortcut — sends an invoice notification via WhatsApp (UTILITY template = free). * * @param tenantId tenant identifier * @param to recipient phone in E.164 format * @param invoiceNumber invoice reference number * @param amount invoice amount * @param currency ISO-4217 currency code (e.g. "USD") * @param dueDate payment due date * @param documentUrl optional public HTTPS URL to the invoice PDF (may be {@code null}) * @return send result wrapping the notification message and optional PDF attachment */ default WhatsAppBusinessSendResult sendInvoice( String tenantId, String to, String invoiceNumber, BigDecimal amount, String currency, LocalDate dueDate, String documentUrl) { return sendBusinessMessage(tenantId, WhatsAppBusinessMessage.invoice() .to(to) .referenceNumber(invoiceNumber) .amount(amount) .currency(currency) .dueDate(dueDate) .documentUrl(documentUrl) .build()); } /** * Shortcut — sends a quotation / estimate via WhatsApp (UTILITY template = free). * * @param tenantId tenant identifier * @param to recipient phone in E.164 format * @param quoteNumber quotation reference number * @param amount quoted amount * @param currency ISO-4217 currency code * @param validUntil date until which the quotation is valid * @param documentUrl optional public HTTPS URL to the quotation PDF * @return send result */ default WhatsAppBusinessSendResult sendQuotation( String tenantId, String to, String quoteNumber, BigDecimal amount, String currency, LocalDate validUntil, String documentUrl) { return sendBusinessMessage(tenantId, WhatsAppBusinessMessage.quotation() .to(to) .referenceNumber(quoteNumber) .amount(amount) .currency(currency) .dueDate(validUntil) .documentUrl(documentUrl) .build()); } /** * Shortcut — sends a payment reminder (UTILITY template = free). * Should be sent a few days before the due date. * * @param tenantId tenant identifier * @param to recipient phone in E.164 format * @param invoiceNumber invoice reference number * @param amount outstanding amount * @param currency ISO-4217 currency code * @param dueDate payment due date * @return send result */ default WhatsAppBusinessSendResult sendPaymentReminder( String tenantId, String to, String invoiceNumber, BigDecimal amount, String currency, LocalDate dueDate) { return sendBusinessMessage(tenantId, WhatsAppBusinessMessage.paymentReminder() .to(to) .referenceNumber(invoiceNumber) .amount(amount) .currency(currency) .dueDate(dueDate) .build()); } /** * Shortcut — sends an overdue-payment alert (UTILITY template = free). * Should be sent when a payment has not been received after the due date. * * @param tenantId tenant identifier * @param to recipient phone in E.164 format * @param invoiceNumber overdue invoice reference number * @param amount overdue amount * @param currency ISO-4217 currency code * @param dueDate original due date * @return send result */ default WhatsAppBusinessSendResult sendPaymentOverdue( String tenantId, String to, String invoiceNumber, BigDecimal amount, String currency, LocalDate dueDate) { return sendBusinessMessage(tenantId, WhatsAppBusinessMessage.paymentOverdue() .to(to) .referenceNumber(invoiceNumber) .amount(amount) .currency(currency) .dueDate(dueDate) .build()); } // ─── Window / status queries ────────────────────────────────────────────── /** * Returns {@code true} if a 24-hour service window is currently open for the * given customer phone. Use this to decide whether a free text message can * be sent without needing a template. */ boolean hasOpenServiceWindow(String tenantId, String customerPhone); /** * Returns the active conversation window for a customer, if any. */ Optional getConversationWindow(String tenantId, String customerPhone); /** * Returns the delivery status of a previously sent message by its local ID. */ Optional getMessageStatus(String tenantId, String localId); // ─── Message history ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── /** * Returns a page of messages for a tenant, ordered newest-first. * Used by Vaadin's lazy {@code grid.setItems(query -> ...)} callback. * * @param tenantId tenant identifier * @param offset zero-based start index * @param limit maximum number of items to return */ List listMessages(String tenantId, int offset, int limit); /** * Returns the total number of messages stored for a tenant. * Used by the grid's count callback when exact row count is needed. */ long countMessages(String tenantId); /** * Returns the most recent {@code limit} outbound messages for a tenant * (convenience method; delegates to {@link #listMessages(String, int, int)}). */ default List listRecentMessages(String tenantId, int limit) { return listMessages(tenantId, 0, limit); } /** * Returns all messages exchanged with a specific customer phone. */ List listMessagesByPhone(String tenantId, String customerPhone); // ─── Templates ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── /** Returns the available templates for a tenant (cached from Meta API or in-memory). */ List listTemplates(String tenantId); // ─── Usage & cost reporting ─────────────────────────────────────────────── /** * Returns messaging usage and cost statistics for the given billing month. * Displayed in the Vaadin cost-optimisation dashboard. */ WhatsAppUsageStats getUsageStats(String tenantId, YearMonth yearMonth); // ─── Webhook processing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── /** * Processes a raw webhook payload received from Meta. * Implementations update message delivery statuses and open/refresh * service windows for inbound messages. * * @param tenantId identifier of the tenant that owns the WABA * @param payload raw JSON string from Meta */ void processWebhookPayload(String tenantId, String payload); }
